observations.title: Sponsor prize release can transfer into a subsequently registered raffle clone
observations.description: Source-supported candidate, low severity and needs human review. Sponsor-recipient screening is performed at creation/initialization against the current same-factory registry. A sponsorRecipient equal to a future clone address is then code-less and unregistered, so it can pass. If that address subsequently becomes another raffle clone before the first raffle returns its NFT, releaseSponsorPrize uses transferFrom to the stored recipient without repeating _isProtocolDestination. A standard ERC721 transfer bypasses the receiving clone receiver hook and ownerOf then confirms the new clone, so the first raffle marks the prize claimed even though the second clone only has release paths for its own configured prize. This violates the stated no movement between raffle clones property and can strand the returned NFT. The quote-token release path does repeat the destination check, making this omission specific to the sponsor NFT return. Impact requires the sponsor-selected future-address recipient; no arbitrary theft from normally configured raffles is established. Defensive property: prize return must reject a recipient that is registered protocol plumbing at delivery time. An execution check remains outstanding.
assumptions: The sponsor selects an as-yet undeployed future same-factory clone address as sponsorRecipient, distinct from the clone being initialized.
That address is deployed and registered before a CashWon or Refunding sponsor-prize return.
The prize is an ordinary standards-compliant ERC721 and differs from the receiving clone's configured prize.
This is a recipient-selection edge case, not demonstrated theft from an honest sponsor who selected an address they control.

gaps: Source-only review: no Solidity compilation, static analyzer, existing tests, generated tests, gas measurement, fuzzing, invariant campaign, solver or formal proof was executed.
Native diagnosis marks configuration unsupported due to gas_reports. Compiler 0.8.36 is outside the documented tested sandbox compiler set (0.8.26/0.8.28/0.8.30).

Docker daemon access was unavailable in the supplementary environment check; no locally usable pinned tool image was established. No test-inclusive plan is permitted without that prerequisite. No tests were supplied in the authorized target.

Clean DESIGN calls arbitrary prize contracts untrusted; IRaffle.sol:13-15 assumes honest standards-compliant prizes. Interface support, callback parameters and ownerOf assertions cannot establish honest escrow/delivery or future transferability of an arbitrary hostile prize. This is a trust-boundary/design limitation, not a separately demonstrated canonical-token exploit.

Canonical USDC and Chainlink wrapper implementations/deployment parameters are not supplied. The consumer base and interfaces are reviewed; canonical identity, deployed max gas/confirmations, billing and callback delivery are unverified.

All 31 selected dependency source files are included and hash-verified. Primary dependency call paths were inspected; unused/transitive library routines were not comprehensively audited. Lockfile relevant package entries were inspected, not all monorepo packages.

Counterfactual and foreign-factory recipients, arbitrary contract recipients unable to operate a ticket or NFT, token pause/blacklist restrictions and unsolicited assets can limit exits. Beyond the documented future-clone prize-return candidate, no additional actionable source-supported fault is claimed.
The supplied target SHA is recorded as operator provenance. No target git history or external repository was consulted to independently authenticate that SHA.
Provider-returned model identity, external usage and spend are unknown. Accepted local selection is gpt-6-astra with ultra effort, fallback disabled; Gebal does not verify that identity.
